findings.observation: RedisConnectionManager calls the base subscribe and unsubscribe methods with argument meanings that do not match the base signatures.
findings.invariant: Derived and base lifecycle methods must agree on argument order and identity domain.
findings.causal_hypothesis: A WebSocket object can be stored where a user identifier is expected, while a user identifier can be stored where a WebSocket is expected, corrupting ownership maps and cleanup behavior.
competing_explanations: An unobserved compatibility wrapper changes the signature before these calls execute.
The derived implementation is unused in deployed runtime.
findings.next_test: Instantiate the derived manager with a deterministic fake Redis and two fake sockets, execute subscribe and unsubscribe, and assert the exact types and identities stored in every local map.

findings.observation: The Redis channel Set is populated with user_id during subscribe but removal attempts use ws_id during unsubscribe.
findings.invariant: A state member must be removed using the same serialized identity domain used to add it.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Redis membership remains after unsubscribe and can create stale presence, incorrect subscriber counts, or zombie subscription state.
competing_explanations: A separate cleanup path removes user_id later.
The Redis Set is diagnostic only and has no delivery or resource effect.
findings.next_test: Capture the serialized Set members before subscribe, after subscribe, and after unsubscribe; require exact return to baseline and inspect later cleanup paths.

findings.observation: Broadcast sends locally and then publishes to Redis, while same-instance suppression in the listener is conditional on test_mode.
findings.invariant: One logical event must reach each intended socket exactly once unless duplication is explicitly part of the protocol.
findings.causal_hypothesis: The publishing instance can process its own Redis event and deliver a duplicate after the immediate local send.
competing_explanations: The Redis client or deployment is configured not to receive self-published messages.
Different subscription maps prevent the echoed path from reaching the same socket.
findings.next_test: Publish one uniquely identified event with test_mode false and assert per-socket delivery count on one and two instances.

findings.observation: The manager supports multiple sockets per user, but disconnecting one socket performs user-wide channel unsubscription without first proving it was the final relevant socket.
findings.invariant: Cleanup for one physical connection must not remove state owned by another live connection or generation.
findings.causal_hypothesis: A late close from an old tab or reconnect generation can remove subscriptions needed by a new live socket, causing an apparently healthy but silent stream.
competing_explanations: Subscriptions are intentionally user-scoped and automatically restored by the surviving socket.
Production guarantees one socket per user despite the set-based data structure.
findings.next_test: Connect two sockets for one user, subscribe, close only the first, then require the second to remain subscribed and receive a unique event.

findings.observation: The total connection gate compares max_connections to the number of user keys, while each key can contain multiple sockets.
findings.invariant: A resource limit must count the resource that consumes capacity.
findings.causal_hypothesis: One or more users can consume more sockets than the configured global connection limit implies.
competing_explanations: A reverse proxy or another layer enforces the true socket limit.
The intended limit is unique users and is merely misnamed.
findings.next_test: Create multiple sockets for one user and compare accepted socket count with the declared global limit and upstream controls.

findings.observation: The clients accept Cookie and arbitrary headers and log the complete headers dictionary after connection.
findings.invariant: Authentication material must not be emitted to console, CI logs, reports, or shared artifacts.
findings.causal_hypothesis: A real session cookie supplied for authorized testing can be copied into persistent logs or captured output.
competing_explanations: The helper is only ever used without credentials.
Logging is disabled in every credential-bearing invocation.
findings.next_test: Add a redaction unit test using a sentinel Cookie and Authorization value and assert the sentinel never appears in stdout, stderr, or logging records.

findings.observation: Cookie and arbitrary sensitive headers can be supplied directly as command-line arguments.
findings.invariant: Secrets should enter through protected environment, file-descriptor, or local session boundaries rather than process arguments or shell history.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Credentials may become visible to process inspection, terminal history, CI command echo, or support transcripts.
competing_explanations: The operating environment prevents process-list and history access.
Only placeholder values are ever supplied.
findings.next_test: Replace secret-bearing CLI values with a local environment or file-descriptor contract and add a regression test rejecting raw Cookie or Authorization command arguments.

findings.observation: Historical helpers contain both object-form subscribeQuotes messages and array-form quotes or orderBook messages.
findings.invariant: A test must bind the protocol version and message contract it is evaluating.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Results from incompatible subscription forms can be compared as though they exercised the same server path, creating false negatives or false confidence.
competing_explanations: The server intentionally supports both equivalent forms.
The object-form helper is obsolete and was never used for final evidence.
findings.next_test: Record server acknowledgements and resulting event types for each form in separate bounded connections; never combine their results without proven equivalence.

findings.observation: The API client exposes real POST and DELETE order methods without a code-level environment allowlist, dry-run mode, confirmation token, or test-account assertion; one test is skipped by marker but the mutating methods remain callable.
findings.invariant: Financial mutations require fail-closed environment and account guards at the operation boundary.
findings.causal_hypothesis: A credentialed integration or ad-hoc script can place or cancel a real order after a test-selection or operator mistake.
competing_explanations: The documented endpoints are mocks or do not exist in the target environment.
The account is a broker-provided sandbox that cannot affect money.
findings.next_test: Do not call the endpoint. Add local tests proving the method refuses to run unless an exact allowlisted non-production origin, test-account identity, explicit mutation flag, and one-time confirmation are all present.

findings.observation: get_session_info returns the raw SID and tests normalize exposing it as ordinary diagnostic state.
findings.invariant: Session bearer material must not be returned by general diagnostics or reporting interfaces.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Callers, logs, notebooks, reports, or debugging output can unintentionally persist a reusable session identifier.
competing_explanations: The SID is not a bearer credential or is independently bound to a protected device.
The method is never called outside isolated tests.
findings.next_test: Replace SID output with redacted presence and digest metadata, then assert no raw sentinel SID appears in diagnostics or reports.

findings.observation: Network requests omit explicit request timeouts, and error paths can log full response bodies and complete captured pytest output.
findings.invariant: External calls must be bounded and sensitive error material must be redacted before logging or artifact creation.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Tests can hang until outer process timeout and can persist tokens, account data, or server diagnostics returned in error bodies.
competing_explanations: The requests Session is configured with an unseen transport timeout.
Server error bodies are guaranteed not to contain sensitive information.
findings.next_test: Inject a delayed fake transport and sentinel secret in an error body; require per-request timeout and complete redaction from all log and report outputs.

findings.observation: Test names, failure messages, suite names, and environment values are interpolated into generated HTML without explicit escaping.
findings.invariant: Untrusted or externally influenced diagnostic content must be HTML-escaped before insertion into a report.
findings.causal_hypothesis: A crafted server response, path, test parameter, or failure message can execute script when a generated report is opened.
competing_explanations: All report inputs are controlled constants.
Reports are rendered in a sandbox that blocks script execution.
findings.next_test: Generate a report with a harmless script sentinel in each interpolated field and assert the output contains escaped text and no executable element.

findings.observation: Documentation reports broad endpoint success while many tests use mocks, integration tests can skip on authentication or 404, and the client notes that endpoint paths require update from actual documentation.
findings.invariant: Mock, skipped, unavailable, and live integration results must be reported as different evidence classes.
findings.causal_hypothesis: An aggregate pass rate can be interpreted as production API validation despite unavailable or unexecuted real paths.
competing_explanations: A separate unpublished live evidence package supports the claims.
The report is explicitly educational rather than an execution record.
findings.next_test: Regenerate the report from machine-readable test outcomes with mock, live, skipped, unavailable, and mutating categories separated and exact run provenance attached.

findings.observation: The bounded public demo stream produced increasing sequence and revision values while last-trade time repeatedly moved backward by approximately 15 minutes across AAPL.US and MSFT.US.
findings.invariant: A client must not treat increasing envelope sequence or revision as proof that every partial market-data field is fresh or from the same producer entitlement.
findings.causal_hypothesis: Real-time and delayed producers may be multiplexed without explicit provenance, or last-trade-time semantics differ across partial producers.
competing_explanations: ltt represents a field whose documented semantics permit the observed alternation.
The demo feed intentionally interleaves delayed and fresh states and clients are expected to distinguish them using an undocumented marker.
findings.next_test: Repeat on an authorized test account with the same two instruments and capture producer, entitlement, snapshot, source-time, sequence, revision, and field-presence semantics; do not place orders.

cross_repository_causal_graph.claim: The analog code patterns supply tests to distinguish duplicate, stale-generation, and ownership mechanisms; they do not identify Tradernet internals.
Protocol-form drift must be controlled before comparing old and current observations.
Credential-bearing retesting should not use tooling that can expose cookies, SID values, or raw sensitive errors.

priority_next_action.action: Build local deterministic regression tests for identity symmetry, two-socket cleanup, self-echo, secret redaction, and financial mutation refusal before any credentialed Tradernet test is considered.
priority_next_action.completion_signal: All negative tests fail on the historical pattern and pass only with explicit identity, generation, redaction, timeout, and mutation guards.
priority_next_action.stop_condition: Do not use real credentials or external financial endpoints in this phase.
